Pick 4 modifications. Mark strongest recommended=true: probably M1 (matched-volume control) as it directly attacks the central confounder and is feasible. Or M2? The most valuable+feasible is M1 combined with M2. I'll recommend M1 (matched-token context control) as the strongest single direction, and mention M2 in it.

Direction: REFINE_SCOPE — narrow to the controlled decomposition (matched-volume + frozen held-out test + context-size sweep) on a text-grounded corpus, since novelty is gone but methodological contribution remains. We introduce the Chinese Data-Text Pair (CDTP), a large-scale Chinese KG-text alignment dataset comprising more than 7 million aligned instances across four broad domains. Each instance pairs a Chinese-language text with one or more textually supported KG triples, totaling 15 million triples. A multi-stage construction pipeline combining alignment filtering, manual verification, and external evidence validation improves semantic consistency and factual reliability. CDTP supports Knowledge Graph Completion (KGC), Question Answering (QA), and Triple-to-Text Generation (T2T). Key evidence for U010:
- CDTP (arxiv:2510.06039): a KG-text alignment dataset where "Each instance pairs a Chinese-language text with one or more textually supported KG triples, totaling 15 million triples" — this is direct evidence that KG–text alignment resources with triple→text provenance exist and can be used for QA, though in Chinese and not the standard English multi-hop benchmarks. It also says SFT on CDTP improves in-domain and OOD robustness.
- SLiNT: injects structural context (pseudo-neighbors) into a frozen LLM with LoRA for link prediction, uses WN18RR/FB15k-237 — mechanism neighbor to the idea but for KGC; SGNE "retrieves pseudo-neighbors to enrich sparse entities and mitigate missing context" — relevant to U012 (family prior art) and to the "context enrichment" mechanism.

So U010: partially resolved. Standard multi-hop benchmarks (WebQSP/CWQ/MetaQA) as retrieved carry no source-passage provenance (analyses of arxiv:2202.13296 and arxiv:2101.03737 show Freebase/MetaQA-based evaluation with no text). But passage-provenance resources exist in other corpora (GraphMERT-extracted disease KGs in 2609.12230; CDTP KG-text alignment dataset in 2510.06039), so the mechanism is constructible, just not on standard benchmarks as-is. Remaining verification: whether any English text-attributed multi-hop KGQA benchmark exists (couldn't search further due to paper budget).

Evidence: quotes from 2609.12230 (size-matched only between diseases p.8; validation edits p.16; repair examples unequal p.15; synthetic QA p.30) and 2202.13296 (subgraph size noise), 2406.09994 (variable triples).

The closest work therefore leaves the decisive control unrun rather than solving it.

input.gap: Passage-local context-triple supervision has not been evaluated on standard multi-hop KGQA benchmarks, because those benchmarks (WebQSP and CWQ over Freebase, MetaQA over a movies KG, as used in the analyzed retrieval and intermediate-supervision works) are not packaged with source-passage provenance for their triples. Text-attributed resources that would make the mechanism constructible do exist elsewhere - triple-to-source-text traceability in GraphMERT-extracted KGs and large-scale KG-text alignment datasets such as CDTP - but they are used for KG completion and text generation rather than for measuring whether context-triple supervision transfers beyond a single synthetic, domain-specific MCQ setting.
input.potential_experiment: Rebuild the context-graph supervision on a text-attributed corpus that ships triple-to-text provenance (e.g., a GraphMERT-style extraction from an open corpus, or a KG-text alignment dataset such as CDTP), generate or reuse open-ended multi-hop questions over it, and evaluate per-hop-depth exact match/F1 against the isolated-triple baseline, a retrieval-based baseline (subgraph retrieval, GNN-RAG-style), and the closest work's MCQ-style protocol.
input.research_question: Does context-triple supervision improve multi-hop KGQA when evaluated with open-ended metrics on a text-attributed KG other than the two disease-specific ones, rather than only on synthetic domain multiple-choice items?
input.verification_required: Whether an English-language text-attributed multi-hop KGQA benchmark with triple-level passage provenance exists was not established: the literature search budget was exhausted before this could be searched, so this must be verified by a further search (e.g., text-attributed knowledge graph QA datasets, document-grounded KGQA) before designing the experiment.
input.why_unaddressed: The works that use standard benchmarks do retrieval or intermediate supervision rather than context-triple supervision, and the work that uses context-triple supervision deliberately avoided standard benchmarks by constructing its own disease-specific, synthetically generated MCQ data with GraphMERT. No retrieved paper attempts the cross-setting transfer, so the external validity of the mechanism is untested rather than refuted.

input.resolution: Narrowed. Standard multi-hop benchmarks as retrieved (WebQSP/CWQ over Freebase in arxiv:2202.13296; WebQSP/CWQ/MetaQA in arxiv:2101.03737) are not packaged with source-passage provenance, and the closest work avoided them by building GraphMERT-extracted disease KGs whose triples are explicitly 'traceable to their originating source text sequence'. However, the mechanism is not restricted to that paper: KG-text alignment resources pair text with textually supported triples at scale (CDTP, arxiv:2510.06039, 15M triples, used for KGC/QA/T2T), so passage-provenance data can be constructed on other corpora. The consequence is that generalization to standard benchmarks cannot be tested with the mechanism as-is, but generalization to a different text-attributed corpus can - a different and more tractable question, now recorded as a gap with a concrete experiment. Remaining verification: whether an English text-attributed multi-hop KGQA benchmark with triple-level provenance exists (search budget was exhausted).

Partially answered for the family question: SLiNT (arxiv:2509.06531) injects KG-derived structural context into a frozen LLM with LoRA for link prediction, retrieving pseudo-neighbors to enrich sparse entities and using contrastive supervision, evaluated on WN18RR and FB15k-237. This is context-enrichment for knowledge graph completion with structural neighbourhoods, not passage-local triples attached to a QA supervision target, so it does not add prior art on the idea's specific mechanism; it does show the mechanism family (inject graph context into an LM) is well populated. CDTP (arxiv:2510.06039) is a KG-text alignment resource with supervised fine-tuning results, again for KGC/QA/T2T rather than the two-regime comparison. No retrieved family member implements the KG-grounded vs CG-grounded supervision comparison.

input.description: Add a supervision-volume control arm to the two-regime comparison: keep the isolated-triple (KG-grounded) instances but pad each with an equal token budget of distractor triples - one variant using random triples from elsewhere in the KG, one using semantically related but non-co-occurring triples chosen so they are not from the same source passage. Compare isolated, volume-matched, and same-passage context arms at matched tokens, matched examples, and matched gradient steps, then attribute any remaining gap to passage locality rather than to more training signal.
input.expected_benefit: Converts the central causal claim from 'context helps' to a falsifiable statement about passage locality at fixed supervision volume, and makes a null or reduced effect interpretable and publishable rather than a failure.
input.experimental_difficulty_basis: Requires additional data-construction work (selecting distractors, verifying token budgets) and at least three training arms per hop configuration, each with multiple seeds; the pipeline itself (SFT on the same backbone and QA items) is unchanged from the existing recipe.
input.implementation_difficulty_basis: Only the training-instance construction changes; no new model, objective, or infrastructure is needed, and the same KG/QA generator is reused.
input.main_risk: Padded distractors may themselves add useful signal or noise that shrinks or reverses the gap, making the comparison sensitive to how padding is chosen; if so, the result is informative but the 'context' effect may be partly explained as generic lexical/structural exposure.
input.potential_novelty: Moderate and hedged: no retrieved work reports a token-matched or example-matched comparison between context-augmented and isolated-triple LLM supervision (G001), but volume controls are standard experimental practice, so novelty lies in the finding rather than the technique.
required_baselines: KG-grounded (isolated triple/path) SFT at matched tokens
input.technical_mechanism: For each target triple, construct three training variants with equal token counts: (a) target triple only plus neutral filler text; (b) target triple plus k randomly sampled triples from other passages in the same KG; (c) target triple plus the k same-source-chunk triples used by the context graph. Train identical SFT runs with a single seed schedule and identical optimizer steps, then evaluate per hop depth. Token counts are verified programmatically before training, and the distractor triples in (b) are additionally tested for semantic relatedness to control for a 'relatedness' rather than 'locality' explanation.
input.title: Matched-supervision-volume control isolating passage locality from added context volume
input.why_differs: The closest work compares KG-grounded vs CG-grounded supervision but does not report a matched-token or matched-example control between those two arms (it size-matches only the two disease KGs against each other); adding a volume-matched and relatedness-matched padding arm distinguishes 'same-passage context' from 'more tokens' and from 'topically related tokens', which no retrieved work does.

input.description: Separate the repair loop from the evaluation it is judged on: freeze a held-out test split before any repair begins, and let the repair loop operate only on a disjoint development split (including its triple quarantine, question regeneration, and validation-set updates). Report accuracy on the frozen test split after every repair round, and also report how many test-set triples would have been quarantined had they been visible to the judge.
input.expected_benefit: Removes the selection/cleaning confound from the repair claim and quantifies how much of the reported 100% one-hop accuracy depends on editing the evaluation data; also yields a reusable protocol for data-cleaning loops generally.
input.experimental_difficulty_basis: Requires only splitting and freezing data plus per-round evaluation on the frozen split; no new training method, and the repair loop is otherwise unchanged.
input.implementation_difficulty_basis: A data-splitting and logging change to an existing pipeline; the main care needed is auditing that no test triple or question enters repair example generation.
input.main_risk: If a large share of the repair gain disappears on the frozen split, the repair component may need to be re-motivated or dropped; the frozen split also reduces data available for repair, which could understate the method's benefit.
input.potential_novelty: Moderate and hedged: the confound is documented in the closest work (it removes invalid triples from and regenerates validation questions) but no retrieved paper quantifies repair gains on a split the loop never edits.
required_baselines: No-repair SFT on the frozen test split
input.technical_mechanism: Partition each hop depth into train, repair-dev, and frozen test splits with disjoint triples. The repair loop may read and regenerate questions only within repair-dev. After each round, evaluate the same frozen test questions and triples, recording accuracy and the count of test triples that the judge independently (blindly) flags as noisy, to bound the selection effect.
input.title: Repair-blind frozen held-out evaluation protocol
input.why_differs: The closest work allows the repair stage to delete invalid triples from, and regenerate questions in, the validation set on which it reports near-perfect accuracy; making the test set unreachable to the loop turns the repair claim into an out-of-sample claim and directly measures the size of the cleaning artifact.

input.description: Replace the binary context/no-context comparison with a dose-response design: sweep the number of attached context triples (for example 0, k/4, k/2, k, 2k) at matched total tokens across arms, and independently sweep context precision (same-passage, same-KG random, semantically related non-passage). Estimate per-hop-depth accuracy curves and test whether the benefit peaks at an intermediate context size, as suggested by work showing fixed larger triple supplies underperform question-fitted ones and that larger subgraphs add noise.
input.expected_benefit: Tests the inverted-U alternative to the monotonic-context assumption behind the original hypothesis, produces a useful design rule for context size in KG supervision, and can explain contradictory outcomes across settings.
input.experimental_difficulty_basis: The sweep multiplies the number of training runs (context sizes x precision conditions x hop depths x seeds) at 14B scale; a reduced-backbone or single-corpus version would lower cost but change the claim's scope.
input.implementation_difficulty_basis: Only the number and selection of attached triples varies; the training and data-generation code is unchanged.
input.main_risk: Compute cost may force a smaller model or corpus, weakening comparability with the closest work; a flat curve would leave the inverted-U question open rather than settled.
input.potential_novelty: Moderate and hedged: context-size control is already an explicit problem at retrieval time (EntropyRAG) and variable versus fixed triple supply has been studied for KBVQA, but no retrieved work runs a supervised context dose-response in LLM KGQA.
required_baselines: Random same-KG context at each size
Semantically related non-passage context at each size
input.technical_mechanism: Attach a controlled number of context triples to each target triple, holding the total token budget constant by padding with neutral filler where necessary so that size and volume are separately manipulable. Fit accuracy as a function of context size and precision per hop depth, and additionally measure whether attached context triples are recoverable as correct reasoning steps at intermediate hops.
input.title: Context dose-response sweep testing the inverted-U (precision versus excess) in supervised KGQA
input.why_differs: The idea assumes more same-passage context helps and that benefit grows with hop depth; adjacent work finds excess context distracts and that fixed larger triple supplies are worse than question-fitted ones, so a dose-response with volume held constant tests a qualitatively different hypothesis than the closest work's two-regime comparison.

input.description: Move the evaluation off synthetic disease-specific multiple-choice items: construct the context-graph supervision on a text-attributed corpus with triple-to-passage provenance (e.g., an extraction pipeline over an open corpus, or a KG-text alignment resource such as CDTP), ask open-ended multi-hop questions, and score with exact match/F1 per hop depth. Include a head-to-head comparison against the strongest alternative answer to the same missing-supervision problem - learned intermediate-step supervision (teacher-student intermediate entity distributions) - at matched budget.
input.expected_benefit: Tests whether the mechanism is domain-general and metric-robust rather than an artifact of generated domain MCQs, and separates two competing remedies for missing multi-hop supervision (added factual context versus added intermediate reasoning supervision).
input.experimental_difficulty_basis: Requires building or adapting a text-attributed multi-hop QA set with open-ended answers, plus implementing an intermediate-supervision baseline and running both at scale; no single off-the-shelf benchmark was confirmed by the retrieved evidence.
input.implementation_difficulty_basis: Needs corpus selection, KG extraction with provenance retention, open-ended question generation or adaptation, and answer parsing; several of these steps were only available in the closest work as an un-released internal pipeline.
input.main_risk: The ported setting may differ from the closest work enough that results are not comparable, and building provenance-preserving extraction is itself error-prone, potentially introducing new noise that confounds the comparison.
input.potential_novelty: Moderate and hedged: context-triple supervision has not been evaluated on standard or open-ended benchmarks in the retrieved literature (G002), but the contribution is transfer evidence rather than a new mechanism.
required_baselines: Retrieval-based multi-hop baseline (subgraph retrieval / GNN-based retrieval)
input.technical_mechanism: Retain the passage identifier for every extracted triple so that context graphs can be rebuilt for any hop path; generate multi-hop questions whose supporting path spans at least three hops; train the same backbone under the supervision arms; evaluate with per-hop exact match and F1, plus a hop-depth breakdown to test whether any context advantage grows with depth outside the MCQ setting.
input.title: Cross-corpus portability with open-ended evaluation and a head-to-head against intermediate-step supervision
input.why_differs: The closest work validates only on two GraphMERT-extracted disease-specific KGs with synthetically generated multiple-choice items; this modification changes corpus, question format, and metric, and pits context-triple supervision against the alternative supervision-enrichment mechanism from the literature rather than only against its own KG-only baseline.

Then reply.

input.direction: Continue the line, but narrow it from 'propose context-augmented supervision plus repair plus lower-hop RL' to a controlled mechanism audit of that already-published recipe: isolate passage locality from supervision volume, evaluate repair on a split the loop cannot edit, and test whether the context effect follows a dose-response with context size and precision, on a text-attributed corpus with open-ended metrics rather than only synthetic domain MCQs.
input.hypothesis: H1' (volume-controlled context): at matched supervision tokens, examples, and gradient steps, same-passage context triples yield higher 3-5-hop accuracy than isolated triples and than volume-matched distractor triples, with any remaining advantage attributable to passage locality rather than added signal. H2' (repair out-of-sample): on a frozen test split never touched by the repair loop, the repair gains shrink to a smaller but measurable amount, bounding the evaluation-set-cleaning artifact. H4' (dose-response): the context benefit is non-monotonic in context size, peaking at an intermediate number of triples, and this peak shifts with hop depth.
input.rationale: KEEP_ORIGINAL is untenable because arxiv:2609.12230 implements the idea's full mechanism - same-passage context-triple supervision, KG- vs CG-grounded SFT, LLM-judged adaptive one-hop repair, lower-hop RL and 3-5-hop evaluation - with method overlap judged 1.0 (C002, C003, C004; U001 resolved). REJECT_DIRECTION is also unsupported: the challenge search found no work that contradicts the assessment that only protocol-level distinctions survive (U011 resolved), and those distinctions are demonstrably unrun rather than settled - the closest work size-matches the two disease KGs but not the two supervision arms, edits the validation set it reports 100% on, allocates unequal repair examples by error type, reports no seed-level variance, and evaluates only synthetic domain MCQ (C006, C007, C009). Adjacent evidence that larger subgraphs add noise and that fixed larger triple supplies underperform question-fitted ones (C005) makes the mechanism's monotonic-context assumption genuinely uncertain rather than merely untested, and text-attributed resources such as CDTP show the mechanism can be ported to an open-ended setting even though standard Freebase-based benchmarks lack passage provenance (U010, G002). A scope refinement therefore leaves a falsifiable, evidence-motivated contribution - a controlled decomposition that could also return a null result - without pretending the original combined contribution is new. It deserves investigation next because it is the smallest change that makes the claims testable and because its controls (matched volume, frozen test split, dose-response) are precisely the ones the retrieved literature has not run.
input.research_question: At matched supervision token budget and on a frozen, repair-blind held-out test split, does passage-local context-triple supervision improve deeper-hop (3-5 hop) KGQA over isolated-triple and volume-matched distractor supervision, and does the effect follow a non-monotonic dose-response in the amount and precision of attached context?
